hook.title: 2,047 components. Mounted 3× faster than Svelte 5.
hook.lede: Svelte compiles components into direct DOM updates. So does Pyreon, from plain TSX instead of a `.svelte` file, and its server rendering came out ahead of Svelte 5 at 10, 100 and 1,000 rows. Miss writing `count++`? Plain Mode lets you.

proof.label: faster to mount a 2,047-component tree: 3.59 ms against 10.80 ms
proof.condition: real Chromium, run 1 table of a two-run record

proof.label: faster compiled SSR at 100 rows (11.64 against 18.08 µs); 1.21× at 10 rows, 1.46× at 1,000
faster swapping two rows in 1,000: 805 µs against 1.50 ms

table.title: Pyreon and Svelte, line by line.
table.note: Synthetic, author-run, Apple M3 Max, real Chromium unless noted. Reproduce: pyreon.dev/docs/benchmarks

rows.rival: 487 / 487 µs (Svelte was the fastest rival); Pyreon 1.08× in both runs
1.75 / 1.71 ms: a three-way tie with Octane

rows.pyreon: `.tsx` functions. Plain Mode (`'use plain'`) lets you write `let count = state(0)` and `count++`.
rows.rival: `.svelte` files with runes, template blocks and scoped CSS.

rows.pyreon: PMTC compiles the same components to SwiftUI and Compose (experimental).

rows.rival: Svelte 5 is a stable major with SvelteKit and years in production.

code.title: The same search box, twice.
code.caption: Svelte's `bind:value` and direct assignment are terse; Pyreon spells the write out. In exchange the component is a TypeScript function, not a second file format.

pyreon.label: Pyreon

code.checked: Svelte side: compiled with the Svelte 5.57.3 compiler, 0 warnings. Pyreon side: typechecked against the repo's `tsconfig` (0 errors), compiled with the real JSX compiler (`transformJSX`) and mounted in happy-dom; typing into the input filters the list.

items.instead: Plain `.tsx`: TypeScript, your linter and your editor read it with no extra language tooling.

pickTheOther.title: When to pick Svelte
items: The smallest output matters more than mount or update cost: the same app is 16.1 KB in Svelte and 17.2 KB in Pyreon.
You like single-file components with template blocks and scoped CSS.
You want SvelteKit and a stable major version with a long production record.

migrate.title: Keep your stores while you move.
migrate.text: `@pyreon/svelte-compat` runs `svelte/store`, lifecycle and context on Pyreon. Components move to TSX.
